blogs.title: When the 'Hidden' Behçet’s Strikes: Navigating Concurrent Systemic and Neurological Involvement
blogs.description: While neurological Behçet’s disease (neuro-BD) typically manifests years after a systemic diagnosis, this case highlights the diagnostic challenge of concurrent presentation. We discuss how to maintain a high index of suspicion for neuro-BD when a patient presents with non-specific CNS symptoms (fever, headache) and subtle mucocutaneous clues like oral aphthae or folliculitis-like rashes, especially when initial brain MRIs appear unremarkable.

blogs.title: Inflammation-Induced SIADH: Is Neuro-Behçet’s a New Player?
blogs.description: The Syndrome of Inappropriate Antidiuretic Hormone (SIADH) is a well-known consequence of CNS inflammation, but its specific link to neuro-BD is rarely discussed. This post explores the potential pathophysiology, specifically the role of pro-inflammatory cytokines like IL-6 in triggering ADH release during acute neuro-inflammatory episodes, and why hyponatremia should be a prompt in the differential for patients with unexplained CNS symptoms.

blogs.title: Beyond the Sodium Level: Hiccups and Rhabdomyolysis as Red Flags for Hyponatremia
blogs.description: Sometimes the most significant clinical clues are the ones we overlook. We analyze how 'soft' symptoms like persistent hiccups and 'hidden' complications like rhabdomyolysis can serve as critical pointers toward profound hyponatremia caused by CNS inflammation. This post encourages clinicians to look for the systemic metabolic consequences of electrolyte disturbances rather than just treating the number on the lab report.

blogs.title: Colchicine vs. Steroids: Rethinking the Management of Acute Neuro-Behçet’s Disease
blogs.description: Corticosteroids are the gold standard for treating neuro-BD, yet this case demonstrates a successful resolution using colchicine monotherapy. We delve into the clinical tension between standard-of-care guidelines and emerging evidence for colchicine's anti-inflammatory mechanisms (inhibiting neutrophil migration and IL-6 production) as a potential steroid-sparing strategy in specific neuro-inflammatory contexts.

blogs.title: The Art of Exclusion: Navigating the Differential for Fever, Headache, and Hyponatremia
blogs.description: When a patient presents with fever, headache, and hyponatremia, the diagnostic path can be a labyrinth of infection, malignancy, and autoimmune disease. This post breaks down the systematic approach to the differential diagnosis—from ruling out common pathogens like HSV/VZV to navigating 'non-specific' markers like sIL-2R and ACE—to arrive at a rare diagnosis like neuro-BD.
